Rashi on Pesachim 77a:11:1.hebrew: סברוה - האמוראין בני ישיבה היו סבורין כן, לפיכך הוצרך להם לישאל הא דבעי לקמיה: לימא מתניתין דלא כר' יהושע:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:11:1.english: They assumed it - The Amoraim, the members of the academy, assumed thus; therefore, it became necessary for them to ask that which [the Gemara] asks further on: "Shall we say that our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua?"

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:11:2.hebrew: דחויה - אף על גב דאכשרה רחמנא למיתי בטומאה, לאו היתר גמור הוא, אלא היכא דלא מישתכחי טהורין. וכיון דלאו היתר גמור הוא, בעי' ציץ לרצויי:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:11:2.english: Overridden - Even though the Merciful One rendered it fit to be brought in [a state of] ritual impurity, it is not a complete permission; rather, [it is permitted] only where ritually pure [people] are not found. And since it is not a complete permission, the frontplate is required to appease [God].

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:12:1.english: Whether it is on his forehead - At the time when ritual impurity occurred with the offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:13:1.english: The High Priest on Yom Kippur shall prove [it] - At the time of the inner service.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:13:2.hebrew: שאינו על מצחו - דהא אין נכנס שם בבגדי זהב, כדאמרינן [בראש השנה] (דף כו.) דאין קטיגור נעשה סניגור:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:13:2.english: As [it] is not on his forehead - For he does not enter there in golden garments, as we say in Rosh Hashanah (26a) that a prosecutor cannot become a defender.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:13:3.hebrew: ומרצה - אם באו בטומאה, דהא קיימא לן כל קרבנות הציבור הקבוע להן זמן דוחין את הטומאה. ורבי שמעון אית ליה טומאה דחויה היא בציבור, ואי לאו משום דציץ מרצה אטומאה, לא הוו מיתכשרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:13:3.english: And it appeases - If [the communal offerings] were brought in [a state of] ritual impurity, for we hold [that] all communal offerings that have a fixed time override ritual impurity. And Rabbi Shimon holds [that] ritual impurity is [merely] overridden for the community, and were it not that the frontplate effects acceptance for ritual impurity, they would not be valid.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:14:1.english: As ritual impurity is permitted in [cases involving] the public - And a communal offering does not require the appeasement of the frontplate, only an individual offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:15:1.hebrew: ודכולי עלמא - כלומר, הנך רבנן דסתם מתניתין סברי אין הציץ מרצה על אכילות, על טומאה שנגע בבשר ובשירי מנחה הנאכלים, אלא על טומאת הדם וקמצים (ואימורין):
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:15:1.english: And everyone [agrees] - That is to say, those Rabbis of the anonymous Mishnah hold [that] the frontplate does not appease [God] for [portions that are] eaten — [that is,] for impurity that touched the meat or the remainder of a meal-offering that are eaten — rather [only] for impurity of the blood, the handfuls [of a meal-offering], (and the sacrificial parts).

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:16:1.hebrew: לימא מתניתין - דאמר עומר ושתי הלחם באין בטומאה, ואף על גב דבעינן ריצוי ציץ, וציץ אאכילות לא מרצי, ונמצא שאין כאן שיריים הנרצין אלא הקומץ לבדו שהציץ מועיל. וכן במיני דמים, לא הועיל ציץ לבשר אלא לדם, וקתני דהדם נזרק:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:16:1.english: Shall we say [that] our Mishnah - Which states [that] the Omer and the Two Loaves are brought in [a state of] ritual impurity; and even though we require the acceptance of the tzitz [headplate], and the tzitz does not effect acceptance for eaten portions — so that there is no accepted remainder here, only the kometz alone for which the tzitz is effective — and similarly with types of blood [offerings], the tzitz was not effective for the meat, only for the blood, and [yet the Mishnah] teaches that the blood is sprinkled.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:16:2.hebrew: דלא כר' יהושע - דאמר אם אין בשר ראוי, אין דם ראוי:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:16:2.english: Not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua - Who says: If there is no fit meat, there is no fit blood.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:16:3.hebrew: אם אין בשר - ראוי, כגון שנטמא או שנאבד, אין הדם נזרק:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:16:3.english: If there is no meat - [that is] fit, such as where it became ritually impure or was lost, the blood is not sprinkled [on the altar].

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:18:1.hebrew: לול - אויר יש בין כבש למזבח. לא היה ראש הכבש מחובר למזבח, שיש אויר מעט בינתים, והמסדר את האברים עומד על הכבש וזורקן על מערכת העצים, לקיים מצות זריקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:18:1.english: A gap - There is a space between [the] ramp and [the] altar. The top of the ramp was not attached to the altar, as there is a small space between them, and the [priest] who arranges the limbs stands on the ramp and throws them onto the arrangement of wood, to fulfill the mitzvah of throwing.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:19:1.english: It is written alongside it: “And you shall eat the flesh” - Thus we see [that] we require [the] flesh to be extant.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:1:1.hebrew: הא לא כתיב בהו מועד - ולא לידחו טומאה, דהא כל קרבנות ציבור ממועד נפקי לן, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:1:1.english: Behold, "appointed time" is not written with regard to them - and [therefore] they should not override ritual impurity, for all communal offerings are derived by us from [the term] "appointed time," as [stated] below.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:2:1.hebrew: קרא עלי מועד - תמוז דשילוח מרגלים מלויי מליוה, וכלו ארבעים דידהו בט' באב — בפרק בתרא דתענית — והוקבעה להם בו בכיה לדורות. ויום עיבור החדש קרי מועד:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:2:1.english: He proclaimed an appointed time against me - Tammuz of the sending of the spies was made full [thirty days], and their forty [days] ended on the ninth of Av — [as stated] in the last chapter of Ta'anit — and weeping for generations was established for them on it. And [the verse] calls the day of the intercalation of the month "an appointed time."

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:3:1.english: And Moses declared, etc. - It is in Torat Kohanim, regarding the Omer and the Two Loaves.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:3:2.english: That we had not learned, etc., regarding which "appointed time" is stated - [Namely,] to override Shabbat and ritual impurity.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:3:3.hebrew: במועדו - משמע לא יעבור זמנן, ואפילו הן טמאין, ואפילו הוא שבת:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:3:3.english: In its appointed time - [This] implies [that] their time must not pass, even if they are ritually impure, and even if it is Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:4:1.english: These you shall sacrifice, etc. - [It] is written in the portion of Pinchas regarding the additional offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:5:1.english: From where [is it derived] to include the omer and what is offered with it - "And you shall offer on the day when you wave [the omer], etc." (Leviticus 23:12).

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:5:2.hebrew: ושתי הלחם - והכבשים הקרבין עמהן, האמור בתורת כהנים, ואינם אמורים בפרשת פינחס:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:5:2.english: And the two loaves - and the lambs that are sacrificed with them, which is stated in Torat Kohanim [Leviticus] and are not stated in Parashat Pinchas.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:5:3.hebrew: ת"ל - בשילהי ההיא פרשתא ד"שור או כשב או עז", "וידבר משה" וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:5:3.english: The verse states - At the end of that passage of “A bull, or a sheep, or a goat,” [it states,] “And Moses declared,” etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:6:1.english: Why do I [need] all these - Let [Scripture] write one, and let these [others] be derived from it.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:8:1.hebrew: שאר קרבנות ציבור - מוספין, דעולה מכפרת אעשה, כדתניא ביומא (דף לו.): אין עולה באה אלא על עשה ולא תעשה שניתק לעשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:8:1.english: The rest of the communal offerings - [These are] the additional offerings, for a burnt offering atones for [the transgression of] a positive commandment, as it is taught in Yoma (36a): A burnt offering comes only for [a transgression of] a positive commandment, or a negative commandment that is rectified by a positive commandment.

Rashi on Pesachim 77a:9:1.hebrew: עומר ושתי הלחם אינן באין אלא להתיר - את החדש, זה במדינה וזה במקדש:
Rashi on Pesachim 77a:9:1.english: The omer and the two loaves only come to permit - the new [grain crop]: this [one] in the provinces [outside the Temple], and that [one] in the Temple.

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:12:1.hebrew: דלא אשכחן תנא דאית ליה טומאה הותרה אלא ר' יהודה - ואם תאמר: מאי אולמא דר"ש טפי מדרבי יהודה? אדרבה, אשכחן במי שהוציאוהו (עירובין דף מו:) דר' יהודה ור' שמעון — הלכה כרבי יהודה! וי"ל דאשכחן לקמן (פסחים דף עח.) ר' יוסי, דנמוקו עמו, דסבר טומאה דחויה היא. תימה לר"י: דבשמעתין משמע דלמאן דאמר טומאה דחויה, אינה דחויה אלא על ידי ריצוי ציץ; ואמאי? הא טומאה דגברא דדחויה בציבור, אע"פ שאין הציץ מרצה על טומאת הגוף, כדתנן בפירקין (דף פ:):
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:12:1.english: For we do not find a tanna who holds that impurity is permitted except Rabbi Yehuda - And if you will say: Why is Rabbi Shimon's [opinion] stronger than Rabbi Yehuda's? On the contrary, we find in [the chapter] Mi Shehotzi'uhu (Eruvin 46b) that [in a dispute between] Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda! And one can answer that we find later (Pesachim 78a) Rabbi Yosei — whose reasoning is [always] with him — who holds that impurity is [merely] overridden. It is astonishing to Rabbeinu Yitzchak: For in our sugya it is implied that according to the one who says impurity is overridden, it is only overridden through the appeasement of the frontplate; yet why [should that be so]? Behold, there is impurity of the person, which is overridden for the community, even though the frontplate does not appease for bodily impurity, as we learned in a Mishnah in our chapter (80b).

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:15:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר אומר הציץ מרצה כו' - רבי אליעזר גרסינן, ולא ר' אלעזר, דלקמן פריך: "וליטעמיך, כיון דאמר ר' אליעזר יש דם אף על פי שאין בשר, הציץ מרצה על אכילות למאי הילכתא?":
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:15:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: The frontplate appeases, etc. - We read [the text as] "Rabbi Eliezer" and not "Rabbi Elazar," for later [the Gemara] asks: "And according to your reasoning, since Rabbi Eliezer says there is blood even though there is no meat, for what halakhic purpose does the frontplate appease for eating?"

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:16:1.hebrew: נימא מתני' דלא כר' יהושע - משמע משום דסבירא ליה דבעינן דם ובשר. ותימה: דאפי' סבירא ליה נמי יש דם אף על פי שאין בשר, כיון דס"ד דטומאה דחויה ואין הציץ מרצה על אכילות, לא אתיא מתני' כוותיה משום שתי הלחם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:16:1.english: Let us say [that] the Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua - This implies [that it is] because he holds that we require [both] blood and meat. And [this is] astonishing: for even if he also holds [that] there is blood even though there is no meat, since we initially thought that [the dispensation for] impurity is [merely] overridden and the tzitz does not effect acceptance for eating, the Mishnah [still] does not accord with him because of the Two Loaves.

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:16:2.hebrew: נימא דלא כר' יהושע - תימה לר"י: והא ע"כ כרבי יהושע אתיא, דקתני סיפא: "ובמוקדשין, אף על פי שנטמא בשר וחלב קיים, זורק את הדם" — משמע: הא נטמאו שניהם אינו זורק, והיינו כרבי יהושע כדאמר לקמן? וי"ל, דה"ק: "נימא דלא כר' יהושע?" — והא ע"כ סיפא אתיא כוותיה, ואם כן קשיא סיפא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:16:2.english: Let us say [the Mishnah] is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua - This is astonishing to Rabbi Yitzchak: surely it necessarily follows Rabbi Yehoshua, for the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teaches: "And in the case of consecrated offerings, even though the meat became impure while the fat remains intact, he sprinkles the blood," which implies that if both became impure, he does not sprinkle [the blood] — and that is in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua, as [the Gemara] states later? And one can answer that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: "[Could] we say [the Mishnah] is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua?" — Why, the latter clause necessarily follows him, and if so, the latter clause poses a difficulty!

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:17:1.hebrew: דם אף על פי שאין בשר שנאמר ודם זבחיך וגו' - תימה לרשב"א: מנא ליה בעולה דיש דם אף על פי שאין בשר? אימא דווקא שלמים, אבל עולה דכולה כליל — אימא אין בשר אין דם; יש דם אף על פי שאין בשר [מנא לן]:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:17:1.english: "Blood, although there is no meat, as it is stated: 'And the blood of your offerings,' etc." - Rashba is puzzled: From where does he [derive] regarding a burnt-offering that blood [is valid] even though there is no meat? Say [that this applies] specifically to peace-offerings, whereas [regarding] a burnt-offering, which is entirely [consumed on the altar], say [that if] there is no meat, there is no blood; [from where do we derive that] there is blood even though there is no meat?

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:18:1.hebrew: אויר קטן היה בין כבש למזבח - בלא אויר נמי היה יכול לקיים מצות זריקה, אלא לכך היה אויר, שע"י כך יזכור לזרוק:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:18:1.english: There was a small gap between the ramp and the altar - Even without a gap [a priest] could also fulfill the mitzvah of throwing [the offering]; rather, there was a gap for this reason: so that through it he would remember to throw [it].

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:1:1.hebrew: שעירי ראשי חדשים איצטריך ליה - תימה, וליתני שעירי ראשי חדשים ולא ליתני אידך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:1:1.english: "It was necessary for [him to mention] the goats of the New Moons" - This is astonishing: let [the Mishnah] teach "the goats of the New Moons" and not teach the other [offerings]!

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:1:2.hebrew: סלקא דעתך אמינא הא לא כתיב בהו מועד - ואע"ג דבפרשת פינחס כתיב נמי ראש חדש, ה"א ד"אלה תעשו במועדיכם" דכתיב בסוף פרשת פינחס לא קאי אראש חדש, אלא אשאר ימים טובים דכתיבי בתריה דאיקרי רגל; דהכי נמי לא קאי אשבת ותמיד, ומצרכי' להו קרא בסמוך:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:1:2.english: It could enter your mind to say that "appointed time" is not written with regard to them - Even though Rosh Chodesh is also written in Parshat Pinchas, I might have thought that "these you shall do on your appointed times," which is written at the end of Parshat Pinchas, does not refer to Rosh Chodesh, but rather to the other festivals that are written after it, which are called regel; for similarly it does not refer to Shabbat and the tamid [daily offering], and [the Gemara] requires a verse for them shortly.

Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:8:1.hebrew: שכן יש בהן צד חמור - פר"ת: שכן ישנן לפני הדיבור, וכמאן דאמר (חגיגה דף ו.): "עולה שהקריבו ישראל במדבר עולת תמיד הואי". ולחם הפנים — אומר ריב"א: מדכתיב "תמיד" ילפינן ליה, דמשמע אפילו בשבת. ובתורת כהנים איכא מאן דדריש דתמיד דחי שבת מדכתב ביה "תמיד", ומיהו מתרי מינייהו הוה מצי למילף כולהו; ואומר ר"י, דשמא יש שום פירכא, דאי לאו הכי אמאי צריך קרא בשאר. וקשה: דבפרק קמא דיבמות (דף ה:) בעי למימר עשה דוחה לא תעשה שיש בו כרת מפסח ותמיד, ופריך: "מה לפסח ותמיד שכן ישנן לפני הדיבור" — ואמאי לא יליף משאר קרבנות ציבור דדחי שבת, כדמסקינן הכא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 77a:8:1.english: "Because they have a stringent aspect" - Rabbeinu Tam explained: [that stringent aspect is] that they existed before the Giving of the Torah [at Sinai], in accordance with the one who says (Chagigah 6a): "The burnt offering that Israel offered in the wilderness was a daily burnt offering." And [as for] the Showbread — Riba says: we derive it from that which is written "continually" (tamid), which implies even on Shabbat. And in Torat Kohanim [the Sifra], there is one who expounds that the daily offering overrides Shabbat from that which is written regarding it "continually" (tamid). However, from two of them one could have derived all of them; and Ri says that perhaps there is some refutation [to such a derivation], for if not so, why would a verse be needed for the rest [of the communal offerings]? And it is difficult: for in the first chapter of Yevamot (5b), [the Gemara] seeks to say that a positive commandment overrides a negative commandment that carries karet [by deriving it] from the Paschal lamb and the daily offering, and [the Gemara] objects: "What [comparison can be made] to the Paschal lamb and the daily offering, since they existed before the Giving of the Torah" — why does it not derive [this] from the other communal offerings, which override Shabbat, as we conclude here?
